disclaimer: Static preparedness guidance paraphrased from official pages. It is not a current evacuation order. Always follow instructions from official responders.

guidance.title: Tornado preparedness and shelter basics
notes: Pick a safe zone at home and work in advance, preferably a basement or small interior room or hallway.
During a tornado warning, go to the safe zone, stay away from windows and do not open them.
Do not try to outrun a tornado in a car; leave the vehicle and seek sturdy shelter.
Keep a battery-powered NOAA Weather Radio for updates.
guidance.attribution: Paraphrased summary; see the source page for the full guidance.

guidance.title: Flood safety basics
notes: Move to higher ground and stay away from flooded areas, especially underpasses, canals and drainage channels.
Do not walk through moving water; six inches can knock a person off their feet.
Do not drive over a flooded road; if a vehicle stalls, abandon it.
guidance.attribution: Paraphrased summary; see the source page for the full guidance.

guidance.title: Earthquake: Drop, Cover, Hold
notes: Indoors: drop to the floor, take cover under sturdy furniture and hold on until the shaking stops.
Outdoors: move to an open area away from trees, buildings, walls and power lines.
If driving, stop safely and do not stop under overpasses or bridges.
guidance.attribution: Paraphrased summary; see the source page for the full guidance.

guidance.title: High-rise fire safety basics
notes: Learn your building's evacuation plan and the sound of its fire alarm.
Call 9-1-1 early; do not assume someone else already has.
If a door is warm, do not open it; if there is smoke in the hallway, return to the room.
Once outside, stay out until the fire department says it is safe.
guidance.attribution: Paraphrased summary; see the source page for the full guidance.

guidance.title: Staying put (shelter-in-place) versus evacuating
notes: If officials tell you to shelter in place or to evacuate, follow the instruction immediately.
Shelter in place means taking immediate shelter indoors when going outside is more dangerous.
When evacuating, use authorized routes and take your Go Bag.
guidance.attribution: Paraphrased summary; see the source page for the full guidance.

guidance.title: How to prepare your family for an emergency
notes: Be ready to care for your household for at least 3 days; city resources may be limited.
Choose two meeting places and identify two separate escape routes from home.
Pick an out-of-area contact person and build an Emergency Supply Kit and Go Bag.
guidance.attribution: Paraphrased summary; see the source page for the full guidance.

guidance.title: OEMC alerts: Notify Chicago
notes: NotifyChicago sends text or email alerts for severe weather emergencies, hazardous materials and traffic impacts.
OEMC also lists a CHILAKE text service for lakefront weather notices.
guidance.attribution: Paraphrased summary; see the source page for the full guidance.
